Analysis: Both hypotheses aim to link SF3B2 overexpression in liver neoplasms to aberrant splicing and downstream oncogenic processes including viral DNA integration. However, Hypothesis 1 focuses on well-established DNA repair regulators (TP53 and RAD51) whose roles in maintaining genomic stability are extensively studied, making the proposed cascade more plausible and easier to test with established tools (e.g., RNA sequencing and splice reporter assays). In contrast, while Hypothesis 2 introduces APOBEC3B along with p53, this addition complicates the mechanistic narrative and may diffuse the focus, as the exact role of APOBEC3B in the context of splicing-driven viral integration is less clearly characterized. Both are safe avenues for research, but Hypothesis 1's emphasis on widely recognized DNA repair genes offers a more straightforward, testable, and mechanistically plausible model with a novel aspect of integrating splicing dysregulation with viral integration in liver cancer progression.
